page: Microsoft Azure F2-1ams_v7 is a single-core virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates comprehensive vector instruction support, including AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16), alongside cryptographic acceleration through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI flags. The system is provisioned with 16.0 GB of memory, yielding an uncommonly high memory-to-core ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent workloads, and no hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural profile of a high-clocked single-core deployment. In single-threaded processing, the server demonstrates exceptional execution throughput, placing in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng workloads (3743.89) as well as single-threaded compression tests, including gzip compression at 38.98 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.88 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 42.75 GB/sec for reads and 32.15 GB/sec for writes, aligning with middle-tier performance profiles. Small-model (135M) language inference registers reasonable throughput at 411.01 prompt tokens per second and 176.95 generation tokens per second.

The strict constraint of a single dedicated thread creates clear performance bottlenecks for multi-threaded and high-concurrency tasks. Multi-core stress-ng performance matches single-core results exactly, ranking in the bottom 25% across broad server comparisons. PassMark aggregate CPU scoring (3478.1), database operations (1477.48), and static web serving throughput (2.77 GB/sec) consistently sit in lower-tier percentiles. Similarly, Redis SET operations are restricted to 3.68 million operations per second. Hardware-level efficiency is heavily tilted toward memory capacity and single-threaded velocity rather than aggregate parallel throughput.

Microsoft Azure F2-1ams_v7 is suited for memory-intensive, low-concurrency workloads that prioritize single-thread clock speed. Practical applications include single-threaded data transformation jobs, memory-heavy batch workers, lightweight caching, and sequential background compilation tasks that do not demand multi-threaded concurrency or local high-IOPS NVMe storage.

Built on the x86_64 architecture with 32 MB of L3 cache, it features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates without GPU acceleration. Performance metrics highlight exceptional single-threaded capability, achieving top-decile scores in single-core stress tests and gzip compression. The resource profile provides a high memory-to-vCPU allocation, making this instance suitable for single-threaded batch data transformations, lightweight caching, memory-intensive analytical processing, and sequential background tasks.
